claims.text: The initial near-equiatomic multi-principal-element automotive alloy catalyst has established catalytic activity but limited durability and poisoning resistance.
A thin high-entropy spinel oxide overlayer can be deposited on the alloy catalyst, for example by atomic layer deposition.
The overlayer can be engineered to have optimized octahedral termination, controlled oxygen-vacancy concentration, and only trace PGM dopants.
Spinel-oxide cation-site distributions and surface oxygen-vacancy concentrations influence catalytic activity.
Octahedral-terminated spinel surfaces are important contributors to catalytic activity.
Subsurface tetrahedral-site cations can induce surface reconstruction and alter catalytic selectivity and performance.
The engineered HESO overlayer will stabilize active sites and prevent deactivating surface reconstruction.
Synergistic interactions among the multiple metal ions in the HESO layer will produce lattice strain and defect engineering.
The overlayer's lattice strain and defects will increase catalytic turnover for CO and hydrocarbon oxidation.
Stabilization of the active oxide phase by the HESO layer will mitigate poisoning by H2O, NO, and sulfur species.
The HESO layer will improve structural resistance to degradation during extended high-temperature and poisoning exposure.
Relative to the unmodified catalyst, the modified catalyst will have lower activation temperatures for oxidation.
Relative to the unmodified catalyst, the modified catalyst will retain higher conversion efficiency in the presence of H2O and NO.
Relative to the unmodified catalyst, the modified catalyst will undergo less degradation during extended aging.
Use of only trace PGM dopants will maintain low platinum-group-metal usage while delivering the claimed performance gains.
The claimed benefits should apply during sub-150 °C cold-start and transient automotive exhaust operation.
Phase change or degradation of the overlayer under extreme thermal cycling could diminish its stability and catalytic enhancement.
Sulfur concentrations beyond standard operational ranges could diminish the overlayer's benefits.
